transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, I just keep thinking that it would be better if I didn't wake up anymore. It's been getting pretty bad, and sometimes I really feel like dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and to my crew at work. So, that's why I'm here.
Have you been hearing any voices or sensing things that others don't, such as a voice telling you that you deserve to be punished?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, it's a man's voice. I hear it coming from right behind me. It happens at job sites when I'm working, or sometimes when I'm just in my kitchen. He says things like, "You missed it," or "Everyone knows." It sounds so clear, exactly as if someone is standing right there behind my shoulder. But whenever I turn around, nobody's there.
Do you hear that voice only during times when you're feeling very down and hopeless, or does it happen even when your mood feels okay?

It happens even when I'm doing a bit better. Like, there was a stretch of several weeks where I was actually getting up, eating a little better, and not crying all day. But I still heard the voice while I was at work. And I stayed completely convinced that the clients and our material suppliers were tracking me. So, no, it doesn't really go away just because I'm not feeling as hopeless.
How long in total, from when it first started until now, have you been hearing that voice and having those thoughts of being tracked?
It's been... I'd say around eleven months total. Yeah, the voices and those thoughts about being tracked through my jobs and messages... they've been happening for about eleven months now.
Out of these past eleven months, roughly how many weeks or months would you say you were experiencing that depressed mood and hopelessness, compared to the time you felt more like your usual self?

I'd say... it's been for most of the time since this all started. Out of those eleven months, the vast majority of it. The guilt, the total exhaustion, just having no interest in anything... and the thoughts about death. They've pretty much been there the whole time. I mean, some weeks were maybe a little less crushing than others, but I haven't really felt like my usual self for almost that entire time.

During that several-week stretch when you were eating and sleeping better and not crying, were you completely free of feelings of sadness, guilt, or worthlessness, or were those feelings still present just to a lesser degree?

Well, like I mentioned before, during that stretch... it was maybe a few weeks where I was eating a bit better, getting out of bed, and not crying all day. I guess the sadness wasn't as crushing right then. But even during those weeks, I was still hearing the voice while I was at work. And I was still completely convinced that the clients and the material suppliers were tracking me. So the sadness was maybe a little better, but those other things didn't stop at all.
Was there ever a time, even briefly, when you were hearing the voice or feeling that people were tracking you but you had absolutely no sadness, guilt, or low mood at all—not even a little?

Well, like I was just trying to say... there was that one stretch of several weeks. My mood actually did clear up then. I was getting up okay, eating a little better, and I wasn't crying all day. I really didn't feel that heavy sadness during those specific weeks. 

But even with my mood feeling normal again, I still heard the voice at work, and I stayed completely convinced that the clients and the flooring suppliers were tracking me. So the low mood was gone for that short time, but those other things were still happening just the same.
Can you tell me exactly how many weeks that stretch lasted when you had no sadness, guilt, or low mood at all, while still hearing the voice and feeling tracked?

I'd say it was exactly three weeks. For those three weeks, the heavy sadness and the guilt were completely gone. I was getting up, eating better, and not crying. But like I said, even though my mood was fine for those three weeks, I was still hearing the voice at work, and I was still totally convinced the clients and the flooring suppliers were tracking me.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms a distinct 3-week period with complete absence of depressive symptoms (mood, guilt, sadness) while psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, delusions of being tracked) persisted unchanged. This satisfies the criterion for psychotic symptoms occurring without mood symptoms for at least 2 weeks, while also confirming that depressive symptoms have been present for the vast majority (most of the 11 months) of the total illness duration. This pattern is classic for schizoaffective disorder rather than schizophrenia (where mood episodes would be brief relative to the psychotic illness) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (where psychosis would not persist independent of mood). F20.9 is ruled out given the substantial proportion of time with concurrent mood symptoms.
